note: The visual plan of the episode: one scene per narration WAV. `say` is the scene's spoken text, already split into subtitle cues; their timing is derived from the generated audio by scripts/narration/regenerate-nicaea-325.ts and lives only in the VideoSpec. The cues of each section, in order, are exactly that section's text in script.json.

say: The First Council of Nicaea, in the year 325.

payload.text: Told from a Catholic perspective.

say: This episode is told from a Catholic perspective.

payload.text: Arius: the Son of God was created.

say: In Alexandria, a priest named Arius taught
that the Son of God was created.

payload.text: There was a time when the Son of God was not.

say: There was a time, he argued,
when the Son did not exist.

payload.text: Alexander rejects the teaching.

say: His bishop, Alexander, condemned this teaching,
and the dispute spread through the East.

payload.text: One empire, one Church?

say: The emperor Constantine, now sole ruler of the empire,
wanted a united Church.
In 325 he summoned bishops to Nicaea,
in today's Turkey.
More than two hundred and fifty came,
most of them from the Greek-speaking East.

payload.text: Pope Sylvester sends two priests.

say: Pope Sylvester was too old to travel,
so two Roman priests took his place.

payload.text: The teaching of Arius is rejected.

say: The bishops rejected the teaching of Arius,
and they set out the faith in a creed.

payload.text: God of God, Light of Light, very God of very God, begotten, not made.

say: It confesses the Son as true God from true God,
begotten, not made.

payload.text: Of one substance with the Father.

say: And it calls him homoousios with the Father:
of the same substance, or being.

payload.text: Why a word not found in Scripture?

say: As Athanasius explained,
biblical phrases alone allowed an Arian reading.

payload.text: Arius and two bishops are exiled.

say: Arius and two bishops who refused to sign
were sent into exile.

payload.text: One common day for all churches.

say: The council also settled Easter:
all churches should keep it on the same day.
And it issued twenty canons on church order,
such as how bishops are ordained.

payload.text: Nicaea did not choose the books of the Bible.

say: Some popular claims are not history.
Nicaea did not choose the books of the Bible.
And the story of Saint Nicholas slapping Arius
is a legend from centuries later.

payload.text: The dispute goes on for decades.

say: Nicaea did not end the dispute.
Arian views found powerful backers for decades.
Athanasius of Alexandria defended Nicaea,
and was exiled five times.
The Council of Constantinople, in 381,
reaffirmed this faith.

payload.text: Still recited in churches today.

say: Its expanded creed is still recited in many churches today.

payload.text: Lives on among the Goths.

say: Arian Christianity lived on among the Goths for two centuries.

payload.text: The first ecumenical council.

say: For Catholics, Nicaea is the first ecumenical council.

payload.text: In Catholic teaching, the Creed of Nicaea is binding dogma.

say: Its teaching on the Son is binding dogma.

payload.text: Catholics profess this faith.

say: Catholics profess this faith in the Creed at Sunday Mass.

payload.text: The same Nicene faith.

say: The Orthodox churches share this Nicene faith,
and honor the council as ecumenical.

payload.text: Confess the Creed as faithful to Scripture.

say: Most Protestants also confess the Creed,
holding it to be faithful to Scripture.

payload.text: Is the Son truly God?

say: Nicaea answered one question for the Church.
Is the Son truly God?

payload.heading: One in being with the Father
payload.takeaway: Nicaea's answer still shapes Christian worship.

say: Its answer, one in being with the Father,
still shapes Christian worship today.
